newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AUSTRALIA SHAREHOLDER GROUP QUERIES ENVESTRA ISSUE.
newsitem.headline: AUSTRALIA SHAREHOLDER GROUP QUERIES ENVESTRA ISSUE.

text.p: The Australian Shareholders' Association (ASA) said on Thursday it was concerned about the level of investor confusion over the prospectus for Boral Ltd's gas distribution spinoff, Envestra Ltd.
ASA executive officer Tony McLean said in a statement the prospectus forecasts distributions at 7.75 percent, 8.15 percent and 8.55 percent for the years 1998, 1999 and 2000.
McLean said it is only when investors read the fine print, do they realise that about two thirds of these distributions are merely repayments of principal initially contributed by them.
Envestra plans to raise A$910 million through the issue of A$350 million of stapled equity securities, A$345 million in term debt, and A$215 million in capital indexed bonds.
Envestra said it was offering 350 million stapled securities at A$1.00 each, with each stapled security comprising one loan note and one share in Envestra.
The loan note and shares will only be able to be sold together and cannot be sold or dealt separately.
Envestra said in its prospectus that initial distributions are be interest paid on the loan note and partial repayment of the loan principal.
"During this period, dividends on the shares are not expected to be paid and accordingly there will be no franking credits available," Envestra said in its prospectus.
Franking credits would only become available when dividends were paid and dividends were not expected to be paid for many years, it said.
The other third of Envestra's distributions are interest payments projected to be 2.53 percent, 3.48 percent and 3.51 percent, McLean said.
McLean said these interest payments are capped and will only be made if there is available cash. Any shortfall in payment of interest in one year will not be made good in future years.
"Many investors are unfamiliar with stapled securities and are struggling to understand the complexities of the Envestra prospectus," McLean said.
"We do not want to discourage people from an investment in Envestra, only to be sure that they are well aware of the returns, the risks and the taxation implications," he said.
Envestra said Boral would buy 19.97 percent of the stapled securities and Boral shareholders would be offered a priority allocation of 60 percent of the securities.
Envestra's offer opened on July 28 and was expected to close on August 15.
The securities were expected to start trading on the Australian Stock Exchange on August 27, it said.
